decisions.executionNote: Approach the nearby cup with the right arm, open gripper and small continuous side-grasp increments; left arm stays home.
Replan from observed pose after continuity rejection: lift and move forward gently to establish elbow-up clearance before descending toward cup.
Use a raised, downward-oriented approach to cup rather than low extension; maintain elbow-up and open jaws.
Angle the open gripper downward above the cup while maintaining clearance; use wrist view to refine centering before descent.
Cup is centered between open jaws in wrist view; descend slowly to its upper sidewall without tilting the contents.
Close around the cup near the rim, then make a small test lift; retention will be checked visually.
Lift cup clear of the tabletop while keeping the grasp closed and the cup orientation stable; inspect that all balls remain contained.
Keep cup raised on the right; begin left-arm approach to reposition the vase toward the shared central area, avoiding a right-arm reach across the left workspace.
Bring the left gripper around to the vase neck from its left side with clearance above the vase; right cup remains steady and closed.
Align the left fingers laterally around the narrow vase neck; descend only gradually while the cup stays stationary.
Fine-align the open left jaws with the vase neck, slightly below its rim, while keeping both elbows up.
Correct the left wrist-view lateral offset and close gently around the vase neck; keep the raised cup steady.
Test the neck grasp by lifting the vase slightly and moving it toward the center, keeping the right-hand cup level and separate.
The vase did not follow the test lift. Reopen and lower the left grasp to the neck sidewall before retrying; keep the cup retained.
Retry the lower neck grasp and a small vertical lift, checking whether the vase follows the left gripper.
Check neck retention with a slow lift toward center; the cup stays raised and closed on the right.
Vase was not retained. Reorient the open left gripper to a steeper neck approach with clearance, avoiding pressure on the broad shoulder.
Center the vase neck in the left wrist view, descend slightly and close the jaws around its upper sidewall.
Test this centered neck grasp by lifting and translating the vase a little toward the center, maintaining closed grippers.
The vase still did not follow. Reopen and adjust the left grasp back and lower so the neck enters the jaw pads rather than only the tips.
Lower the open left pads another small amount around the visible neck and close without lifting yet.
Test the deeper vase-neck grip with a small raised translation toward center; keep both grippers closed.
Leave the vase on the table and withdraw the left hand. Bring the retained cup inward for a controlled handoff, keeping the arms on their own sides.
Approach a central handoff: the left open gripper faces the cup side, while the right carries it inward upright. Keep clearance above the vase.
Bring the left open jaws toward the lower cup sidewall for a central handoff, leaving the right grip closed and the cup upright.
Back the left hand away for clearance and turn the right wrist around the upright cup, presenting its side for a safer handoff.
Continue presenting the cup from the right while the left hand advances toward its lower side, open and clear of the right fingers.
Advance the left open fingers around the lower cup wall, with the right hand supporting it steadily during handoff alignment.
Close the left fingers on the cup, pause for seating, then open the right hand for the handoff without moving either wrist.
Withdraw the open right gripper slowly to verify that the left hand retains the cup and all seven balls.
The cup was not retained in the handoff and is lying on the table. Clear the left hand and approach it cautiously with the open right gripper to recover it.
Follow the cup's new resting location with the open right gripper, lowering toward its sidewall; keep the left hand clear.
Center the right jaws on the lying cup's sidewall and close slowly, without rolling it farther.
Test whether the cup is now retained with a small vertical lift. Some balls have spilled, so full transfer is not yet achieved.
Raise the recovered cup clear of the table while moving the left hand to the vase's left side, preparing a gentle central repositioning.
The cup remains on the table, not grasped. Reopen and descend toward its lower sidewall with corrected height, keeping the left hand clear.
Track the cup's shifted position and lower the open right pads around the body, avoiding a premature high grasp.
Correct the wrist-view lateral offset and close around the cup body at the lower height; several balls remain spilled on the table.
Lift slowly to verify this rim/body grasp visually before attempting to right the cup. The spilled balls still require recovery.
The cup still did not lift. Reopen and shift the right wrist outward so the finger pads, not just the wrist projection, align with the cup.
Use the wrist image to center the lying cup between the open right pads, correcting the lateral and height offsets before closure.
Close the right pads around the centered cup body and make only a small test lift, checking visual retention before further motion.
Lift the closed right grasp slowly to confirm that the cup follows; the spilled balls are still on the table and must be recovered.
The cup is visibly retained. Lift it while gradually rotating its mouth upward, compensating wrist translation to keep the cup clear of the table.
Continue rotating the retained cup upright at clearance height; spilled balls remain on the table and are not yet transferred.
Move the retained empty cup toward a clear table area for placement, while withdrawing the left arm. The seven spilled balls still require recovery.
Lower the empty cup toward table support without releasing prematurely; continue returning the left hand toward its home region.
Set the empty cup down gently and open the right hand; complete the left arm's retreat toward home.
Withdraw from the placed cup and reorient the open right gripper for recovering spilled balls; leave the left arm at home.
Align the right gripper above a spilled ball near the center-right table, with the fingers approaching downward and the left arm stationary.
Lower toward the centered spilled ball and begin closing only near table height, keeping the left arm home.
Lift away from tabletop contact with the right jaws closed and inspect whether a ball is retained before transporting it.
No ball retention is visible. Reopen and change to a near-vertical approach above a separated ball for more precise recovery.
Refine the near-vertical right-hand approach over the isolated ball using the head and wrist views; leave jaws open for alignment.
Use the observed wrist-image motion to bring a single ball between the right jaws before lowering further.
Fine-center the isolated ball at the closing pads, lower slightly, and close the right gripper for a careful recovery attempt.
Test the closed ball grasp with a slow lift and slight motion toward the vase; judge retention from the camera views.
No retained ball is visible. Reopen and align a vertical approach directly over the isolated ball using its calibrated head-view location.
Refine the open-jaw alignment from the wrist image, bringing the nearer ball toward the center of the pads with a slow shallow descent.
Fine-center the ball between the vertical pads, close fully, and make a small test lift to check retention.
The previous ball rolled out rather than being retained. Reopen and align above the separated ball using the calibrated head view, at a slightly lower grasp height.
